analysis: What changed vs Tuesday's 9 AM brief: the waiting room got a fresh catalyst overnight, and it is chips, not macro. SK Hynix's more than sevenfold profit jump (operating profit up about 630% year over year) lifted Micron, Sandisk and Western Digital premarket and kept the Nasdaq futures bid alive, extending Tuesday's tech-led session (Nasdaq +1.18%, S&P +0.60%, Dow essentially flat). The second overnight story, OpenAI reportedly planning to buy Google TPUs, is thinner: one outlet, no terms, no company confirmation, so it reads as a sentiment tailwind for Alphabet into its own print rather than a confirmed demand order, and it sits awkwardly next to Nvidia's own premarket gain. The earnings-grading regime from Tuesday carried straight into the after-hours tape: Robinhood, Visa, Seagate, NXP and Enphase all fell despite beats in several cases, because margins, guidance or costs disappointed, while PPG and Manhattan Associates jumped on raised outlooks. Signal: memory/AI-hardware demand is still the tape's engine, and today's double event (Fed hold widely expected at 2:00 p.m. ET, then Microsoft and Alphabet after the close) will test whether cloud growth and capex plans justify it. Noise: single-stock after-hours percentage moves, the OpenAI-TPU report until confirmed, and any single 10-year print near 5% while sources straddle 4.98-4.99%. The Fed backdrop also shifted in tone from Tuesday's brief: the market now prices a hold at about 96%, with the debate moved to a possible December hike, not a cut.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Premarket split: at 04:53 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were down 88 points (-0.17%), S&P 500 E-minis up 7.25 points (+0.1%) and Nasdaq 100 E-minis up 122 points (+0.41%), per Reuters.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tech futures are leading into the open while Dow futures lag — the same tech-led split as Tuesday's session, not a broad risk-on open.

headlines.headline: SK Hynix reported a more than sevenfold jump in quarterly profit (operating profit up about 630% year over year to 83.33 trillion won); Micron gained 4% premarket, SK Hynix's US-listed shares jumped 7.8%, Sandisk rose 0.8% and Western Digital 4.5%, with Nvidia up 0.8%, AMD up 1.5% and Marvell up 1.7%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A memory-chip earnings blowout is lifting the whole AI-hardware complex premarket — demand evidence, not just sentiment, behind the chip bid.

headlines.headline: Alphabet rose 1.2% premarket after The Information reported, citing a person familiar with the matter, that OpenAI plans to buy Google's tensor processing units (TPUs); no financial terms were disclosed and neither company confirmed the plan.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile: a TPU order would be a new demand stream for Google's chips, but until confirmed it is a pre-earnings sentiment lift, not a booked order.

headlines.headline: Microsoft and Alphabet both report after today's close — Microsoft fiscal Q1 (consensus roughly $90.6B revenue, about $4.71-4.73 EPS, with Azure guided to 45% constant-currency growth) and Alphabet Q3 (consensus roughly $127.9-128B revenue, about $2.94-3.03 EPS, with Google Cloud projected near $29.15B after 82% growth last quarter).
headlines.why_it_matters: Cloud growth versus capex is the day's real test — both prints land hours after the Fed decision, so guidance will set Thursday's tone.

headlines.headline: The Fed concludes its two-day meeting today with the decision at 2:00 p.m. ET and a press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET; prediction markets price a hold at about 96% (hike about 5%, cut about 1%), with the rate currently 3.75%-4.00% after September's hike.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hold is the priced-in base case, so the market-moving part is guidance on December — a hawkish steer matters more than today's decision itself.

headlines.headline: Robinhood fell about 8.2% premarket to around $86.84 after Q3 EPS of $0.51 missed the roughly $0.55 estimate, even as revenue rose 12% to $1.42B; crypto transaction revenue fell 55% year over year to $120M and operating expenses rose 16% to $739M.
headlines.why_it_matters: Profit miss plus a shrinking crypto-trading line outweighs revenue growth — the same strict grading that hit Tuesday's reporters.

headlines.headline: Visa slipped about 2% after hours even as adjusted earnings and revenue topped estimates, as non-GAAP operating margin of 66.6% narrowly missed the 66.7% consensus.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat that still falls — a margin miss of a tenth of a point was enough to send a Dow stalwart lower, showing how tight grading is this week.

headlines.headline: After-hours grading stayed harsh elsewhere: Seagate fell about 6% despite a fiscal Q1 beat (non-GAAP EPS $7.68 vs $7.43 expected, revenue $4.2B) and above-consensus Q2 guidance; NXP fell about 9% on in-line Q4 revenue guidance; Enphase fell about 14% as Q4 revenue guidance of $225-255M trailed the $297.6M estimate. Counterpoints: PPG jumped about 7% and Manhattan Associates about 10% on raised outlooks.
headlines.why_it_matters: Guidance, not the reported quarter, is deciding after-hours moves — beats are being sold when the outlook disappoints, and raised outlooks are the only reliable lift.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: Tuesday's session closed with the S&P 500 up 0.60% to 7,722.60, the Nasdaq up 1.18% to 26,477.81 and the Dow up 0.03% to 52,377.57; Tesla led the Magnificent Seven, up 4.04%, Amazon gained 1.61%, Apple 0.93% and Alphabet 1.19%, while Meta fell 1.64% and Microsoft 0.24%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tuesday's tape was already tech-led before the overnight chip news — the premarket move extends that session rather than reversing it.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: Meta's enlarged equity fundraising reached $97.5B (including $25B of common stock at $625 and $12.5B of mandatory convertible preferred at $50, plus a potential $60B future Class C program), with Nvidia investing $3B in the offering and deepening its Muse AI partnership with Meta.
headlines.why_it_matters: The dilution overhang that made Meta Tuesday's megacap laggard is still live — Nvidia's backing softens the story without removing the share-supply question.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. The Q3 distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized, ~8.4% yield) went ex-dividend Monday Oct 26 and pays Nov 6. Q3 earnings arrive before the open Tue Nov 3 with an 11 a.m. ET call. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. Background: on Oct 1 the partnership issued 34.5M non-convertible Class A units at a fixed 9.25% annual distribution rate in an internal reorganization, and it now trades on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) after moving from NYSE on Oct 5. WTI back above $101 premarket keeps the energy backdrop supportive with no company-specific catalyst.

After today's close: Microsoft (fiscal Q1) and Alphabet (Q3) — watch Azure/Google Cloud growth and capex plans, not just EPS.
Thursday Oct 29 after the close: Amazon (est. about $2.00 EPS, about $202B revenue) and Intel; Monday Nov 2: Apple reports.
OpenAI-TPU report: watch for confirmation or denial from either company — unconfirmed until then.
10-year yield near 5% and WTI above $101: whether either breaks higher into the Fed decision and changes the risk tone.
